subject: mathematics_2b
question_text: If a point P is moving such that the lengths of tangents drawn from P to the circles x² + y² − 4x − 6y − 12 = 0 and x² + y² + 6x + 18y + 26 = 0 are in the ratio 2 : 3, then find the equation of the locus of P.

mark_split.label: Replace each tangent length by S₁₁

insider_note: Squaring the ratio is the whole method: PT₁ : PT₂ = 2 : 3 becomes 9(PT₁)² = 4(PT₂)², and the 9 goes with the FIRST circle — putting the 4 there is the single commonest slip on this question.

steps.label: Write the ratio condition
steps.margin_note: One mark. Cross-multiply first, then square; squaring the fraction directly is where the 9 and the 4 get swapped.
steps.memory_tip: The length of the tangent from P to S = 0 is √S₁₁. So a ratio of lengths is a ratio of square roots.
lines: Let P(x₁, y₁) be a point on the locus.
PT₁ = length of the tangent from P to
PT₂ = length of the tangent from P to
steps.why: Tangent lengths are square roots, so the condition is squared to remove them. Cross-multiplying before squaring keeps the 9 attached to the first circle and the 4 to the second.
common_mistakes: Squaring 2/3 to 4/9 and then multiplying the wrong side.
Writing PT₁ = S₁₁ instead of PT₁ = √S₁₁.

steps.label: Replace each tangent length by S₁₁
steps.margin_note: Second mark. S₁₁ is just the left side of the circle equation with the point substituted — no halving, no sign change.
steps.memory_tip: S₁₁ = x₁² + y₁² + 2gx₁ + 2fy₁ + c. Put the point into the circle as it stands.
steps.why: The square of the tangent length from an external point is S₁₁, which is the whole left side of the circle equation evaluated at that point. No rearranging is needed.
common_mistakes: Using √(g² + f² − c) instead of S₁₁.

steps.label: Simplify to the locus
steps.margin_note: The last two marks. 9 − 4 = 5 stays in front of x² and y², so this locus is a circle, not a line.
steps.memory_tip: 9 − 4 = 5, so the second-degree terms survive and the locus is a circle.
steps.why: The x² and y² terms do not cancel here because the multipliers 9 and 4 differ, so 5x² + 5y² is left and the locus is a circle. Its coefficients 5, 60, 126 and 212 share no common factor, so the equation cannot be reduced.
common_mistakes: Dividing the final answer by 5 and producing fractions.
Expecting a straight line. That happens only when the two multipliers are equal, so the x² and y² terms cancel.
